background: Raiffeisen Bank International is the central institution of the Austrian Raiffeisen cooperative banks and a leading lender across Central and Eastern Europe, with a large and long-running exposure to Russia that it has been unable to fully exit.
synthesis: Two of the three agencies rate the bank, A on average and the weakest of them at A-, one on a positive outlook and one on stable, the last move a one-notch upgrade by one of the three on 11 Jul 2023. On the figures it is among the better-capitalised names in the EU and Nordic set: CET1 of 17.3% is above the peer median and leverage of 8.5% in the top quarter, with LCR of 151% at the median and NSFR of 139% in the top quarter. Leverage has added 0.6 points since 30 Jun 2024 and LCR has given up 31 points since 30 Jun 2025, CET1 and NSFR broadly flat, on figures to 30 Jun 2026. The caveat is not in the ratios but in the newsflow: the Russian business and the litigation around it account for most of what has been flagged in the last 90 days, the most recent a default judgment won on 22 Sep 2026.
